map.Shannon-Wiener 多样性指数 H = −Σ(pᵢ × ln pᵢ)，: Shannon-Wiener diversity index H = -Σ(pᵢ × ln pᵢ), where pᵢ = the individual count of species i ÷ the total individual count; the larger H is the higher the diversity (2 to 4 is common in forest communities). Pielou evenness J = H ÷ ln S (S being the number of species) runs from 0 to 1, and the closer to 1 the more even it is. Simpson dominance D = 1 - Σpᵢ². Margalef richness R = (S - 1) ÷ ln N (N being the total individual count). Used together, the four indices fully characterize the community structure.
